Ransomware Attack Disrupts French Automotive Firms, Including Renault SA

A large-scale ransomware attack has struck several major automotive manufacturers and suppliers in France, disrupting IT systems and halting production lines at multiple sites. Renault SA confirmed on Thursday that it is among those affected, as the cyber incident continues to unfold across the sector.

The attack, which began late Wednesday evening, targeted company networks with a sophisticated ransomware strain that encrypted critical data and demanded payment for decryption keys. According to sources familiar with the investigation, at least three major firms—including the supplier group Automeca Solutions—have reported significant operational impacts.

Renault SA issued a brief statement Thursday morning: “Renault SA is currently experiencing technical disruptions due to a cyber incident affecting our IT infrastructure. Our teams are collaborating closely with authorities to contain the situation and restore operations as quickly as possible.”

Production activities at Renault’s Flins plant northwest of Paris were temporarily suspended, according to a spokesperson for the CGT union. “Workers were sent home as soon as the IT systems went down. The management told us they are not sure when production can safely resume,” said CGT regional representative Laurent Dubois. “It’s a real blow, especially as this comes during a critical period for vehicle deliveries.”

Industry analysts say the incident is one of the most serious cyber attacks to hit France’s automotive sector in recent years. “Automotive manufacturing depends heavily on interconnected IT systems, from supply chain management to robotics on the production line,” said Marie Chevalier, cybersecurity analyst at HexaCert Conseil. “A disruption of this magnitude can quickly cascade into lost output, delivery delays, and financial losses running into millions of euros per day.”

The French Association of Automotive Suppliers (F2A) called for urgent action to help affected companies. “This attack underlines the need for robust cyber resilience across the sector,” F2A president Christophe Martin stated. “Our members are working around the clock to restore operations, but the full impact is not yet clear.”

While details of the attack’s origin remain under investigation, French government cybersecurity agency ANSSI said it is providing technical support to the companies involved. A spokesperson noted, “We are coordinating with the affected firms to contain the spread of the malware. At this stage, there is no indication that customer data has been compromised, but assessments are ongoing.”

As the situation develops, automotive assembly and supply chain operations remain disrupted at multiple sites. Companies are urging partners to remain patient as they work to restore normal activity. “Our priority is to ensure the integrity of our systems and the safety of our employees,” said Renault SA’s spokesperson.
